synopsis: OSI provides domain-neutral sensor and ground-truth interfaces that the research finds transferable to off-road work, and the glossary lists it among open standards for connecting simulation tools [f7166, f15862]. Chapter 9 recommends OSI and FMI/SSP for sensor and model interfaces, with adapters to simulation, HIL and physical automation; the glossary also recommends requiring OSI export in simulation-tool RFPs [f7203, f16487]. Persival offers a concrete implementation pattern: OSI sensor models packaged as FMUs and correlated against real sensor output, while requesting an OSI-packaged black-box FMU is one of five options when suppliers withhold sensor internals [f15948, f16495]. ASAM's 2025 high-fidelity OSI project extends sensor interfaces and runs until March 2027, coinciding with the program's planned first tool-chain integration [f7169, f15870]. Despite these findings and recommendations, the research explicitly says it did not verify OSI's status, leaving a verification gap relevant to interface planning [f7165].
